title: Background jobs holding the community-wide lock block moderator goal creation
current: When a moderator submits the create-goal form while posts-updater work holds the community-wide lock, creation fails immediately with an 'already in progress' message. Deletion waits up to 4 s, then fails the same way.
evidence: One lock, subscriber_goal_community_mutation_v1_lock, is taken at 13 call sites, including work run by posts-updater-job every minute (completed-goal cleanup, highlight reconciliation, app repair, scheduled-post displacement, source-post deletion, onboarding). Manual creation passes no retry option. The lock's 60 s TTL (userFacingLockTtlMs) can outlive a job killed at the 30 s request limit. Characteristics: A, D.
outcome: Reported by the maintainer: form progression appears stuck while the cron job runs. Not yet confirmed in logs.
assumptions: That job phases hold the lock long enough to collide with moderator actions in practice.
That Devvit doesn't separately queue requests behind a long-running scheduler request (not checked in the docs).
investigate: How often and how long does each job phase hold the lock? Use the #237 lock timing logs.
Are 'already in progress' rejections logged, with the holder's workflow?
Does a killed job leave the lock until the TTL expires?
Per AGENTS.md, check the Devvit docs: can a long-running scheduler request delay other requests to the same installation?
Would a short bounded wait (like delete's 4 s) on manual creation fix the symptom?
reuse: withCommunityGoalMutationLease already accepts a retry option { maxWaitMs, intervalMs } (used by the delete route).

criticality.why: Moderator-visible: it can block goal creation for up to a minute with an unhelpful message.
